segments.text: Listening Test In the listening test, you will be asked
to demonstrate how well you understand spoken English.
The entire listening test will last approximately 45 minutes.
There are four parts and directions are given for each part.
You must mark your answers on the separate answer sheet.
Do not write your answers in your test book.
Part 1.
Directions For each question in this part, you will
hear four statements about a picture in your test book.
When you hear the statements, you must select the one statement that best describes what
you see in the picture.
Then find the number of the question on your answer sheet and mark your answer.
The statements will not be printed in your test book and will be spoken only one time.
Now part 1 will begin.
Number 1.
Look at the picture marked number 1 in your test book.
A. The men are shaking hands.
B. The men are wearing jackets.
C. Some cups are being stacked on the table.
D. Some pastries are being placed in a display case.
Number 2. Look at the picture marked number 2 in your test book.
A. Some leaves are gathered into piles.
B. A man is sitting in the table.
Sitting on a bench.
C. The trees are being trimmed.
D. Branches are hanging over a walkway.
Number 3. Look at the picture marked number 3 in your test book.
A. A pedestrian is climbing some steps.
B. Some planters have been lined along a curb.
C. Some workers are watering plants.
D. A door has been left.
Left open.
Number 4. Look at the picture marked number 4 in your test book.
A. Some books are stacked on a cart.
B. Some books are spread out on a table.
C. One of the women is standing at a shelf.
D. One of the women is opening a box.
Number 5. Look at the picture marked number 5 in your test book.
A.
He's zipping up a backpack.
B. He's standing on a driveway.
C. He's riding on a highway.
D. He's holding on to his cap.
Number 6. Look at the picture marked number 6 in your test book.
A. He's slicing bread on a cutting board.
B. He's putting on an apron.
C. He's arranging sandwiches
on a tray.
D. He's wiping down a counter.
Part 2.
Directions.
You will hear a question or statement and three responses spoken in English.
They will not be printed in your test book and will be spoken only one time.
Select the best response to the question or statement and mark the letter A, B or C on your answer sheet.
Now, let us begin with question number 7.
Number 7.
Where did Bridget put the floor plans for the client meeting?
A. She stacked them on the drafting table.
B. So the client could review the layout.
C. A long line at the print room.

Which song did you want me to mix first?
A. Thanks.
I appreciate the update.
B.
With the studio microphone.
C. The valid we recorded yesterday.

Number 11.

A. The tripod handle came loose.
B.
Yes, right around 3.
C. Two reflectors and a backdrop.

B. Your room key is ready at the front disk.
C. There's a restroom with mirrors just past the elevators.

A. The panel meets again on Thursday morning.
B. You'd better check with the electrician.

B. A premium wash package.

B. They're trying out a new sound system.

A. My cousin's been looking for kitchen work.

C. They hired a new dishwasher last month.

A. We can push the deadline back.
B. A permanent position, I believe.
C. He'll be hard to replace.
Number 18.

B. Boarding begins at gate 14.
C. I printed mine at home this morning.
Number 19.

B. I know, scheduling the placement interviews will take weeks.
C. Applicants can pay the fee online.

B. The picture books just came in.
C.
I was actually going to suggest the same thing.

Number 23.

Number 24.

B. I ended up skipping it.
C. Yes, I signed up.
Number 25.

A. The courier picks up at four.
B. On the shelf by the loading door.
C. Yes, I've packed them already.
Number 26.

A. Traffic was jammed near the entrance.
B. Just three books and a DVD.
C. I'll go find a technician right now.
Number 27.

A. To visit my grandfather.
B. Yes, the heart tests came back fine.
C. The information desk can help with that.
Number 28.
Will you be at Saturday's park cleanup?
A. Sure, it was last Saturday.
B. Yes, I'll see you there.
C. It's parked out front.
Number 29.
Could you print the agenda copies before the meeting starts?
A. About 15 attendees so far?
B. The printer's out of toner.
C. You should submit it by Friday.
Number 30.
How do I submit my monthly expense report?
A. Anything over $50 counts?
B. Before the 5th of December,
C. You'll need to email the receipts to accounting.
Number 31.
Why did Ramona move up the start time for today's delivery shift?
A. Because a big client needs an early drop-off.
B. She shifted the boxes to the back.
C. The van wouldn't start this morning.
Part 3.
Directions.
You will hear some conversations between two or more people.
You will be asked to answer three questions about what the speakers say in each conversation.
Select the best response to each question and mark the letter A, B, C, or D on your answer sheet.
The conversations will not be printed in your testbook and will be spoken only one time.
Questions 32-34 refer to the following conversation.
Good morning, and welcome to Bramwell Watch Repair.
How can I help you today?
Hi, I'd like to drop off this watch for a look.
It stopped running last week.
It was actually my grandfather's. He passed it down to me not long ago, so I'd really like to get it working again.
Of course, a stopped watch is usually a straightforward job, most often just the battery or a small internal part.
We can normally have it ready in about three business days.
And I should mention, all of our repair work comes with a guarantee, so if anything goes wrong after you collect it, just bring it back and we'll sort it out.
That's good to hear. How long does the guarantee actually last?
Six months from the day you pick up the watch.
Here's a leaflet with the full terms. It explains exactly what's covered.
Number 32. What did the man recently do?
Number 33. What are the speakers mainly discussing?
Number 34. What does the woman give to the man?

Hi, I like to book a haircut and color for Saturday afternoon.
I've been going to Lydia for a while now, so I prefer her if she's available.
Let me check. I'm sorry. Lydia is fully booked on Saturday.
Julian has an opening at one o'clock though. That's about an hour earlier than the afternoon slots.
He does haircuts and color as well. Would you also like to add a deep conditioning treatment after the color?
One o'clock would Julian sounds fine. I'll pass on the treatment this time. Money's a bit tight this month, but maybe next visit.
No problem. You're booked for Saturday at one. Please arrive about ten minutes early to fill out a short form,
and I'll send you a text message confirmation shortly.

Questions 38-40 refer to the following conversation.
Hi, Preston. I wanted to catch you before the end of the day. I'll be out all next week at the annual marketing conference,
and there's a client presentation schedule for Wednesday afternoon. Would you be able to cover it for me?
Sure, I can do that. Just let me know. Which account is the meeting for?
It's the Halveson Retail account. We've been working on their campaign proposal for about a month now,
and the slide deck is basically finished. All the talking points are in the notes as well.
Great. That helps. Could you send me the deck a couple of days beforehand? I'd like to go through everything
and review the numbers before I stand up in front of them.

Questions 41-43 refer to the following conversation.
Good morning. You must be here to pick up your weekend camera rental. Is it under the name Barlow?
Yes. Kenneth Barlow. I reserved the standard video camera kit with two lenses.
I'm shooting a short film this weekend.
Great. I have your booking right here. Actually, before I bring it out, a newer model just arrived at our shop this week.
It has better low light performance, which could really help on your shoot.
Hmm. It does sound useful, but I'm working with a tight budget on this project. I planned everything around the standard rate.
I understand. But the weekend rate is the same for both cameras, so the upgrade wouldn't cost you anything extra.
Oh. In that case, I'll definitely take the newer one. One more thing. Do you have a lightweight tripod I could add on?
Yes. We have several available. I'll set one aside for you.
Here's the equipment checklist. Please look it over before you leave, just to make sure everything's on it.

Number 43. What does the woman give the man? Questions 44 through 46 refer to the following conversation.
You know, ever since that productivity workshop last week, I keep thinking we should try that scheduling tool I saw, Sink Point.
Our team wastes so much time on back and forth emails just to book a simple meeting.
That does sound useful. My only worry is our department software budget is already fully committed for this quarter, so we can't purchase anything new right now.

Would you be willing to set up the team account?
Sure. Glad to. I'll register us online right after this meeting. Everyone should have the invite link by end of day.

Okay, that covers the budget items. So before we wrap up, I'd like to talk about scheduling the mandatory compliance training we need to run this quarter.
Oscar, when would work best for your team?
Well, my department is right in the middle of our peak workload this month, so I'm hoping we can push the session to sometime next month instead.
I'd have around 40 people attending from my side.
That makes sense. Fiona, what are your thoughts?
I agree with Oscar. Next month is much better for us as well.
Before we lock in a date, though, we should check which of the larger meeting rooms are open, because a group that size definitely won't fit in one of the standard rooms.

Elliot, I just finished the first draft of the logo for Marigold Tea Room, and I'd really like your eyes on it before I send it over.
They want to review it first thing tomorrow morning, so I want to make sure it's solid.
Sure, let me have a look.
Overall, I think the layout works really well. The one thing I'd change is the background color.
That dark green feels a bit heavy for a tea room. I'd go with something softer, maybe a warm cream.
You're right. That would suit the brand much better. I'll adjust the color and resend the file to you before the end of the day.

Questions 59 through 61 refer to the following conversation.
Hi, good afternoon. I'm Gina Talbot. I'm here to pick up my car. I dropped it off first thing this morning for the oil change.
Welcome back, Miss Talbot. Yes, the oil change is all finished, and your car is parked right out front.
Here's your invoice. You can settle up at the counter whenever you're ready.
Thanks. So, did everything else look okay when they had it up on the lift?
Mostly, yes. But our technician did flag one thing during the routine inspection. Your front brake pads are wearing down quite a bit, closer to the end of their life than we'd normally like to see.
So, we'd recommend having them replaced fairly soon.
Oh, I see. How urgent is that, and what would it cost, roughly?
I'd say sometime within the next month is a safe window, and the estimate for parts and labor comes to around $240.
I'd be happy to book that appointment for you right now, if you like, and just so you know, we also run a free courtesy shuttle on the day, so you won't have to sit and wait.

Good afternoon, high-veil coffee traders. This is Denise Kimball speaking.
Hi, Denise. My name is Anton Delgado. I'm opening a new cafe downtown next month, and I'd like to set up a wholesale account with your company for our beans.
Wonderful. Welcome. We roast right here in the city and shipped to cafes across the whole region, so most of our customers are within a day's drive of the roastery.
And the one thing they tell us they appreciate most about us is our delivery speed.
Any order placed before noon goes out the same afternoon and reaches you the next morning.
That sounds perfect for what I need. I've been looking through the price sheet you emailed me, and I'd like to start with 40 kilograms of the mountain blue blend.
Can I send you a signed purchase order later today?
Of course, please do. I'll process it as soon as it comes through.

Question 65 through 67 refer to the following conversation and floor plan.
Hello, is this Ms. Corbett? This is Nathan calling from the Linden Court Hotel.
I'm phoning about the meeting room you reserved with us for Thursday afternoon.
I'm afraid we've run into a small problem, and I wanted to speak with you as soon as possible.
Yes, this is Ms. Corbett speaking. What seems to be the matter?
We've got 12 people coming in for a team planning session, and I really need a quiet space where we can work through the whole afternoon without interruption.
I completely understand. The issue is that the air conditioning unit in your room has stopped working, and our maintenance team can't get the replacement part until Friday morning.
So we'd like to move your booking to a different room on the same floor. Would that be all right with you?
Yes, that's fine. As long as it's roughly the same size. Could you tell me which rooms are still open?
I think there's a floor plan attached to the confirmation email. I'm looking at it now.
Of course, if you look at the plan, you'll see four numbered rooms along the main corridor.
Two of them are already taken this week, one by a training group and another by a small industry meeting.
So those are marked as occupied. That leaves two rooms for you to choose from.
I can see them. Honestly, my preference would be a room with a window.
We'll be in there for about five hours, and a bit of natural light really does make a difference for that kind of long session.
In that case, there's really only one that fits. The other open room is on the interior side of the corridor, so it has no outside view at all.
I'll transfer your booking to the one on the exterior wall right now and send you an updated confirmation by email.
Number 65. Why does the woman need the meeting room? Number 66. What does the woman agree to do?

Question 68 through 70 refer to the following conversation and chart.
Meredith here. Glad you stopped by. I've finished writing up the new incoming shipment inspection procedure,
and I can walk you through the chart if you have a few minutes.
Sure, please do. Remind me what we're trying to fix with this. Why did the team put it together in the first place?
The main goal is to catch any damaged goods before they reach our inventory.
As you can see, we've broken the whole thing into four stages on the diagram.
Okay, one quick question. The drivers keep asking me when they're actually free to leave the loading bay.
At what point in the procedure do we release them?
Right here on the flowchart. The rule is we sign off on their paperwork once the pallet check is complete,
and that's when they can pull out of the bay.
Goss it. I'd like to go through the rest with you, but not right now.
I have to lead the nine o'clock safety briefing in a few minutes.
Number 68. What are the speakers mainly discussing? Number 69.
Look at the graphic. When can the drivers leave the loading bay?

Question 71 through 73 refer to the following excerpt from a meeting.
Good morning everyone, and thanks for coming to this month's operations meeting.
As many of you know, we've had a run of complaints lately about not being able to tell customers exactly where their shipments are once the trucks leave the yard.
To fix that, we're rolling out a new tracking system called RootScan.
The main thing it does is give us a live map view of every package from pickup to delivery,
so anyone at a desk can answer a customer's question in seconds.
RootScan goes live across the warehouse next Monday.
Before then, every one of you needs to complete a short online training module
that walks you through the new handheld scanners and the updated labeling steps.
The deadline for finishing the training is this Friday at 5 o'clock,
and I really do mean Friday because the old system gets switched off right after that.
You'll find the module on our staff portal under the tab marked training.
If you run into any trouble logging in, drop a note to the help desk and they will sort it out for you.
Number 71.
What news does the speaker share with the listeners?
Number 72.

You're listening to KVRT Community Radio, your home for local events and neighbourhood news.
